New York

8 directory entries · Research in progress

  • Cayuga↗Historical and continuing homeland connection
    Connection & source
    Historical and continuing homeland connection

    Actual homeland paragraph explicitly identifies Finger Lakes, New York. Only geography used; unrelated legal timeline claims not adopted.

    Historical and continuing; geography passage inspected 2026-10-21. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

    Read the supporting source ↗
  • Haudenosaunee↗Continuing constituent nation connection
    Connection & source
    Continuing constituent nation connection

    Actual Cayuga Nation homeland paragraph identifies Cayuga as a founding Haudenosaunee nation and locates its homeland in New York. Confederacy-level link through a constituent nation; not every Haudenosaunee homeland or one interchangeable people. Additional canonical entry has no originalId.

    Historical and continuing; selected actual passage inspected 2026-10-21. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

    Read the supporting source ↗
  • Lenape↗Historical homeland connection

    Nation's overview names parts of New York. Not statewide territory.

    Ancestral geography; community account. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

    Read the supporting source ↗
  • Montaukett↗Dated state legislative account of a continuing Long Island community
    Connection & source
    Dated state legislative account of a continuing Long Island community

    The New York State Assembly member’s statement explicitly identifies the Montaukett Indian Nation as part of the Long Island community in its account of a New York recognition proposal. This supports a New York community connection; the bill’s proposal is not presented as enacted law. Inspection: Actual dated statement, HTML lines 25–32, inspected. Limits: The statement is advocacy by a legislator and is attributed as such. No present state or federal recognition conclusion, current leadership claim or historical court conclusion is adopted. A court’s former extinction assertion is not used as evidence of people’s disappearance.

    Community described in a March 24, 2025 legislative statement. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

    Read the supporting source ↗
  • Onondaga↗Nation published historical place connection
    Connection & source
    Nation published historical place connection

    Brad Powless's Nation-published historical account explicitly locates Onondaga Lake in present-day central New York. Only that broad geographic connection is indexed; the account is not used to assign a precise confederacy formation date.

    Public content inspected 2026-10-21. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

    Read the supporting source ↗

    Connection & source
    Specific government and historical community connection

    The Nation explicitly places its historic and continuing communities in New York. This concerns the Seneca Nation's account rather than identifying every Seneca government with that institution.

    Public content inspected 2026-10-21. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

  • Shinnecock↗Present community center location
    Connection & source
    Present community center location

    The Nation publishes its Shinnecock Community Center in Southampton, New York, with citizen historian Shane Weeks's account. No ancient population or settlement-age estimate is adopted.

    Public content inspected 2026-10-21. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

    Read the supporting source ↗
  • Tuscarora↗Present government location
    Connection & source
    Present government location

    The Nation's own page gives its office at Lewiston, New York, and separately gives a Lewiston address for the Nation School. Inspection: Nation Office and Nation School public contact sections. Limits: Present New York institutional location only. This does not substitute for research on the North Carolina homeland, migration, or distinct contemporary communities.

    Public Nation office location inspected 2026-10-21. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

    Read the supporting source ↗

These are starting lists, not a complete census. Modern borders help you navigate; they are not Indigenous homeland boundaries. A connection may be historical or present-day and does not imply presence throughout a region. Directory names can overlap; the profiles explain their relationships.
